launches.body:
**TL;DR:** AI hardware trades over phone calls and forwarded spreadsheets. No venue, no price to mark against: lenders mark billions in GPU collateral off appraisals. We're building Stoa, an RFQ marketplace where buyers and sellers get firm quotes within 48 hours, and settled trades build the prices the market can mark, finance, and hedge against.

<https://youtu.be/zbD21BgAo88>

GPU deals close in group chats. We know because we've been in them.

A price arrives as a voice note. Someone forwards an inventory list, then it gets forwarded again, and soon three brokers are offering the same machines. Nobody knows who actually owns what or whether any quote is firm.

The market behind those chats is worth hundreds of billions of dollars a year. Lenders mark billions in GPU collateral off appraisals, not trades.

We're Berat, Eren, and Kaan. We're building Stoa.

AI hardware is becoming an asset class, but its market is missing the basics: a venue where hardware can trade, prices that buyers, sellers, and lenders can mark against, and eventually financing and hedging built on those prices. We're starting with the venue: an RFQ marketplace for GPUs. It gets buyers and sellers firm quotes, and every bid and settlement builds the history the rest needs.

**Here's how it works**

Post what you want to buy or sell: B300s, H200s, H100s, a bare card or a full cluster, new or secondary.

Vetted dealers bid blind with firm quotes. Instead of spending weeks calling around, you get through the RFQ in 48 hours.

We handle the unglamorous parts too: KYB and counterparty checks, contracts, shipping, and settlement.

In our first month, $300M+ in RFQs ran through the book.

**Why the marketplace comes first**

Ask what an H100 is worth and everyone you call gives you a different answer.

On Stoa, dealers quote against the same RFQ without seeing each other's bids. Because every RFQ, firm quote, award, and settlement runs through us, we see what the hardware actually trades for.

A quote is an opinion. A settled trade is a receipt.

That transaction history becomes prices buyers, sellers, and lenders can mark against. Once marks are grounded in settled trades, financing and hedging can follow.

Platts started printing oil prices in a magazine. Kelley Blue Book began as one dealer's published list of what he'd pay for cars. GPU inventory is still being passed around in forwarded spreadsheets, and Blackwell upgrades are now pushing H100 fleets into the secondary market.

Someone is going to be the price.

**The team**

We've known each other for more than ten years. We have founded companies, traded interest rate derivatives, and built trading and pricing infrastructure for oil and gas. Now we're building it for AI hardware.

Hi, we're Computable, the first exchange for physical compute where you can buy, sell, and use GPU capacity for exactly the dates you want like staying on Airbnb. You pay less, commit less, and stay flexible.

<https://youtu.be/6HTjUUO__MU>

**The problem**

Compute is the newest major commodity, but it still trades like an asset from the last century. You overpay going in and you eat the weeks you don't use.

**How it works**

We put a public price on every week. Open the market and you'll see dedicated H100 nodes, every week through January 2027, each with its own price, from $2.55/GPU-hr. Pick a start week and an end week, and it's yours.

* **Buy the exact weeks you need.** Two nodes for the last two weeks of October is just a few clicks, and you never pay for weeks you don't want.
* **Sell back what you don't use.** If your plans change, sell the weeks back to the market whenever you want; we keep a market quote posted on every position.
* **Lock next year at a price you can see.** January 2027 is on the grid today, so you know exactly what the future run costs before another H100 40% rate jump happens.
* **Real machines, fast.** Dedicated H100 SXM nodes, full SSH root access, live within an hour of your window start.

**Why us**

Our founding team comes from Jump Trading, Coinbase, Citadel Securities, and other trading firms and exchanges. We have spent our careers building markets. Stay tuned for more products coming soon as we build out the financial infrastructure of the AI economy.

**Our asks**

* **Open [market.getcomputable.com](http://market.getcomputable.com) and buy GPU!**
* **Tell us what to list next: GPU type, region, dates.** Email [team@getcomputable.com](mailto:ray@getcomputable.com); it directly sets what goes on the grid.

# The market for specialized data locked up in enterprise companies.

[Petrarch](http://petrarch.co) is unlocking enterprise data for tomorrow's economy.

<https://youtu.be/YRflyEOuVYo>

Frontier labs scraped the internet dry. Then, labelers contracted subject matter experts to hand-make data. Now demand has shifted towards the bespoke data locked up within industries like construction, manufacturing, and logistics.

Petrarch targets companies with valuable **operational** **data** they haven't monetized, from **legacy** **businesses** and **startups** to companies undergoing **bankruptcy** and **pivots**.

Petrarch **sources** suppliers, **cleans** and **restructures** the datasets, certifies **legal clearance**, and resells to **applied AI startups and labs.** They have already transacted construction plans, autonomous driving recordings, and codebases.

With experience at Scale and Meridian AI, founders Ian Lee, Samuel Hahn, and Sudhish Swain dropped out of Harvard to unlock the next wave of training data.

If you need proprietary datasets or think you have something valuable on your hands \
(or recently pivoted), reach out at [founders@petrarch.co](mailto:founders@petrarch.co) or visit us at [Petrarch.co](http://Petrarch.co)!
